modelSelectorBlock.title: Model Selector
modelSelectorBlock.description: Compare models by speed, quality and cost, with extended thinking and web search.
modelSelectorBlock.compositionBody: Uses Popover, Button, Avatar, Command and Switch. The dropdown contains the model list and two conversation settings directly, using Popover's own surface and shadow. Colors, typography, spacing, radii and motion come from the existing component library. LobeHub Icons supplies Claude logos for Opus, Sonnet and Haiku; Auto retains its automatic-selection symbol. The panel is capped at 360px, while the preview's InputMessage composer retains its original 512px maximum width; both shrink for narrow viewports. The selector connects through InputMessage's leftSlot.
modelSelectorBlock.dataContractBody: Pass models with stable unique IDs, descriptions, icons and optional 1–5 relative ratings. A higher cost rating means more expensive. The controlled value contains modelId, extendedThinking and webSearch; onValueChange returns the complete next value. Optional latency and pricing metadata remain available to host applications, while this dropdown displays only model choices and settings. Use labels for localized copy. The screenshot-based demo models and ratings are illustrative fixtures.
modelSelectorBlock.behaviorBody: Use arrow keys to navigate models and Enter to choose. Selection closes the popover and restores trigger focus; Escape or an outside click dismisses it. Keyboard highlighting follows host selection changes and resets on reopening without replacing the focused input. Choosing the current model closes without a redundant change event. Screen readers receive descriptions and ratings, with the committed model marked separately from keyboard highlighting. Settings update immediately and keep the panel open. Supports controlled or uncontrolled opening, disabled options, an empty list and missing selections. The panel fits narrow viewports; its inner content scrolls when needed while the Popover shadow remains visible. Host applications own model requests and persistence; the preview submits locally without contacting a model service.
